hints: Substitute $x = 6$ into the derivative $\frac{dy}{dx} = 12\left(\frac{1}{2}x - 1\right)^{-4}$ to find the gradient $m$.
Use point-slope form $y - 4 = m(x - 6)$ to write the equation of the tangent at $P(6, 4)$.
walkthrough:
Evaluate the gradient of the tangent at $x = 6$:
$$\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=6} = 12\left(\frac{1}{2}(6) - 1\right)^{-4} = 12(3 - 1)^{-4} = 12(2)^{-4} = \frac{12}{16} = \frac{3}{4}$$

Write the equation of the tangent at $P(6, 4)$ using point-slope form:
$$y - 4 = \frac{3}{4}(x - 6) \implies y = \frac{3}{4}x - \frac{1}{2} \quad (\text{or } 3x - 4y = 2)$$

ai_rubric.Tangents and Normals: Substitutes $x=6$ to evaluate gradient $m = \frac{3}{4}$ (M1). States tangent equation $y - 4 = \frac{3}{4}(x - 6)$ or $y = \frac{3}{4}x - \frac{1}{2}$ (A1).

skill_tags: Finding a Curve from Its Derivatives

hints: Integrate $\frac{dy}{dx} = 12\left(\frac{1}{2}x - 1\right)^{-4}$ with respect to $x$ using the reverse chain rule.
Divide by the derivative of the inside function ($\frac{1}{2}$) and include constant of integration $+c$.
Substitute $P(6, 4)$ into the curve equation to solve for $c$.
walkthrough:
Integrate the derivative using the reverse power and chain rules:
$$y = \int 12\left(\frac{1}{2}x - 1\right)^{-4} dx = \frac{12\left(\frac{1}{2}x - 1\right)^{-3}}{-3 \times \frac{1}{2}} + c = -8\left(\frac{1}{2}x - 1\right)^{-3} + c$$

Substitute the coordinates of point $P(6, 4)$ to determine $c$:
$$4 = -8\left(\frac{1}{2}(6) - 1\right)^{-3} + c = -8(2)^{-3} + c = -8\left(\frac{1}{8}\right) + c = -1 + c$$
$$c = 4 + 1 = 5$$

State the final equation of the curve:
$$y = -8\left(\frac{1}{2}x - 1\right)^{-3} + 5 \quad \left(\text{or } y = 5 - \frac{8}{\left(\frac{1}{2}x - 1\right)^3}\right)$$

ai_rubric.Finding a Curve from Its Derivatives: Integrates correctly to $-8(\frac{1}{2}x - 1)^{-3} + c$ (B2). Substitutes $(6, 4)$ to solve for $c = 5$ (M1). States curve equation $y = -8(\frac{1}{2}x - 1)^{-3} + 5$ (A1).
